summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman was admitted for worsening bilateral leg pain, redness, and swelling, initially concerning for cellulitis, but found to be due to chronic lymphedema with venous stasis changes. Despite prior outpatient treatment with IV furosemide and clindamycin, her symptoms progressed, prompting hospitalization for diuresis and infection evaluation. IV vancomycin was started but discontinued after no improvement and negative blood cultures, with dermatology attributing findings to stasis. A CT scan ruled out abdominal masses but revealed new renal lesions requiring outpatient MRI follow-up. Diuresis with IV furosemide and metolazone was limited by rising creatinine, leading to discontinuation. She was treated for sinusitis with levofloxacin and oral thrush with nystatin. Her INR was optimized on warfarin, and a brief non-epileptic event was noted. She was discharged home with services on oral diuretics, with instructions to monitor weight, follow up with her PCP, and complete imaging for renal lesions.
